claims.statement: Jiang explains the 1688 settlement as a strategy to protect Dutch capital by moving wealth to England under parliamentary power.
claims.status: Attributed explanatory model; magnitude of wealth transfer unverified
claims.nextTest: Compare Dutch and English financial records; test the claim that most wealth or all gold moved.

claims.statement: Jiang presents the 1694 bank and parliamentary backing as shifting lending risk from an individual king to an enduring nation.
claims.nextTest: Read the 1694 Charter and loan legislation; distinguish contractual liability from modern sovereign-debt language.

claims.statement: Jiang links geographic security and the navy with trade, intermarriage, religion and Freemasonry as mechanisms of trust.
claims.status: Attributed connections; particular networks undocumented here
claims.nextTest: Identify named actors, dates and records for each proposed historical relationship.

claims.statement: Jiang associates property protection and contract law with England becoming a financial refuge, then compares modern financial centres.
claims.status: Author analogy; chronology and legal causation not established
claims.nextTest: Locate specific legal texts and dated capital-flow evidence; avoid treating the Locke caption error as a verified name quotation.

claims.statement: Jiang argues that inward capital and financialization can produce inequality, corruption and eventual social decline.
claims.status: Author causal model; not an empirical finding of this packet
claims.nextTest: Test country-specific capital-flow and distribution data against competing explanations.

claims.statement: In answering a student, Jiang contrasts family and community values with competitive pressures that make states adopt strategies he considers destructive over time.
claims.nextTest: Separate the student question from Jiang’s answer; identify explicit model assumptions and falsifiable predictions.

claims.statement: The Bank of England describes its 1694 founding and an initial £1.2 million government loan for war with France.
claims.locator: JP-S03 founding section; JP-S04 catalogue introduction
claims.status: Narrow institutional corroboration; not proof of JP-C01–06
claims.nextTest: Inspect original Charter, loan legislation and subscriber records.
